title: Modernize networking helper modules for cross-cloud IP lifecycle and adapter-based provider bindings
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Over the years our networking terraform modules accumulated provider-specific assumptions (AWS EIP lifecycle, AZ-centric NAT attachments, and provider-pin side-effects) that cause plan churn across workspaces and block multi-cloud experiments (Azure/GCP). This ticket refactors the small-but-high-impact helper modules that manage ephemeral/persistent public IPs, NAT/egress attachments, and cloud-specific tagging to a provider-adapter pattern. Goals: 1) Abstract provider-specific implementations behind a stable intent API so workspace code expresses "attach ephemeral public egress" or "reserve persistent public ip" without cloud bindings. 2) Separate lifecycle strategies (transient vs persistent) to reduce destructive apply noise and avoid unnecessary replacements. 3) Provide an adapter layer for AWS/Azure/GCP that is unit-testable and easier to add new providers. 4) Reduce provider version upgrade friction by isolating provider calls to adapter modules and reducing cross-module provider aliasing. 5) Improve plan times by enabling parallel apply semantics and smaller state churn in common paths.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Existing workspaces in aws-prod and aws-staging apply without replacing persistent public IPs when using the new modules (no unexpected recreate). 2) Introduce an Azure adapter and demonstrate a greenfield workspace provisioning a load-balanced public endpoint with the same intent API. 3) Unit tests for adapter logic and a terraform plan smoke test in CI for all supported providers. 4) Documented upgrade/migration steps for teams in Confluence and an automated script that updates the minimal callsites in our monorepo. 5) A measurable reduction in median plan time for common networking changes by >=15% in a representative workspace (compare before/after CI runs).
migration_plan: Phase 1 (safe refactor): Add new helper modules under modules/networking/intent/ with stable inputs and an adapter interface. Implement AWS adapter that delegates to existing ip and nat resources; keep old modules as compatibility shims. Phase 2 (canary): Convert two non-critical workspaces (dev-dns and perf-test) to call the new intent modules and validate no resource replacements. Phase 3 (provider expansion): Add Azure adapter implementation and create a greenfield azure-workspace to validate. Phase 4 (cutover): Provide automated codemod script to update callsites, deprecate old modules after 2 cycles, and merge provider pin simplifications. Rollout: create toggle variables to switch between legacy and intent modules per-workspace for safe rollback.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Implicit semantics in older modules may rely on side-effect ordering leading to subtle diffs. Mitigation: Keep compatibility shim and run parallel plan comparisons and state diffs before apply. Risk: Provider API differences (e.g., ephemeral IP attach semantics) could cause transient downtime during migration. Mitigation: Canary on low-traffic workspaces, perform attaches in outside maintenance windows, and use live smoke tests. Risk: Provider upgrade required to support adapter features causing broader plan churn. Mitigation: Isolate provider calls into adapter modules so provider version bumps are scoped and can be rolled independently.
